title: Audit Events Playbook: Dual-Write & Schema Evolution v0.9
summary: Working playbook for safely evolving the audit/event JSON schema, coordinating SIEM exports, and linking events to evidence bundles during the RBAC v2 migration. Focused on operational steps, compatibility rules, and consumer coordination.
goals: Establish a clear versioning model and gating for breaking changes
Define change categories and required remediation steps for consumers
Describe a dual-write rollout pattern and monitoring expectations
Provide pragmatic SIEM mapping guidance and evidence-automation linkage rules
scope: Applies to newline-delimited JSON audit events emitted by control plane services (API gateway, auth, deployer, scheduler, evidence automation). Excludes application debug logs and telemetry metrics.
assumptions: Primary audit stream is ndjson; downstreams ingest newline-delimited JSON
We will not rename fields in-place for existing major versions; transforms are used for SIEM
RBAC v2 introduces immutable role IDs; events must reference both id and display name
versioning_model: Semantic-like versioning: major.minor.patch. schema_major integer present on every event for quick downstream gating. Major increments signal breaking changes requiring migration and dual-write.
change_rules: Additive: optional fields or widened enums. Increment minor; no consumer action normally required.
Compatible transform: internal renames keep legacy aliases for at least one minor release; announce deprecation in changelog.
Breaking: structural field changes require major bump, migration guide, and minimum 30-day dual-write with observed metrics before deprecating old shape.
backport_strategy: Security fixes and small additive fields backported to the last two supported service releases. New evidence fields launched behind feature flags with dual-write to avoid forcing immediate consumer changes.
rbac_v2_considerations: Canonical actor representation: actor_id (UUID), actor_type (user|service|api_key), actor_display_name, actor_org_id must be present on RBAC-related events.
Role reference: include role_id (immutable UUID) and role_name. On role-change events include prior_role_snapshot and new_role_snapshot as compact JSON strings for evidence.
Permission context: for sensitive ops include permission_context array of permission strings (e.g., 'serve:create').
evidence_automation: Events that are part of an evidence bundle should set evidence_bundle_id and evidence_storage_path (s3:// or gs://).
Finalization events from evidence automation should include signed_manifest_url and signed_manifest_hash (sha256).
Signer metadata: signer_id and signer_certificate_ref should be added by the signing pipeline for chain-of-trust verification.
siem_mapping_guidance: Avoid changing primary audit field names; implement a transform layer for SIEM that maps to ECS-like fields.
Suggested mappings: event_type -> ecs.event.category; actor.id -> ecs.user.id or ecs.service.name depending on actor_type; actor.ip -> source.ip; outcome -> event.outcome; request_id -> event.id.
Flatten nested snapshots into top-level string fields (e.g., evidence.prior_role_snapshot_raw) to accommodate SIEM indexing limitations.
Publish both timestamp (RFC3339) and timestamp_epoch_ms to improve ingestion reliability.
compatibility_matrix: v1.x consumers accept new optional fields. Events tagged schema_major=2 must be dual-written until consumers upgrade. Monitor parse-failure-rate and consumer drop-rate during rollout.
rollout_checklist: Publish changelog and migration guide and notify known downstream consumers.
Implement feature flags and dual-write in all producing services.
Add compatibility metrics: parse-failures, consumer-errors, delivery-latency.
Run 14-day canary dual-write in high-internal-traffic region, then expand to full-dual after review.
After minimum 60 days of healthy dual-write, schedule removal of legacy aliases or pipeline as appropriate.
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert if parsing errors > 0.1% in a rolling 24h window.
Alert if downstream subscription lag > 5 minutes for > 5% of partitions.
Produce weekly compatibility digest for consumers and integrations.
open_questions: Do we standardize an actor.subject_claims blob for OIDC vs. expanding actor fields?
Should evidence bundles live in per-customer immutable buckets or shared bucket with per-bundle ACLs?
What is the rotation policy for signer_certificate_ref to satisfy legal chain-of-custody?
notes_for_reviewers: Working draft: reviewers owning consumers should list required fields and parsing limits (max depth, max field length). Focus feedback on dual-write windows, schema_major gating, and SIEM flattening guidance.
